handoffs.what: Make sure a stuck output device cannot pin decoded audio. On this Mac's device sink the AudioContext clock sits at 0.01 s; the tracker reads it as running, and the client never suspends or closes it. Scheduled stop() calls never fire, so every looping bed source stays a pending activity and keeps its buffer: 657-672 MB of AudioBuffers at Home after two matches (mus_menu x3, mus_postgame x2, mus_match_<map> plus _intense). That alone puts RIFT as the second match at 3225-3239 MB on the device sink, against 2779-2797 MB on the fake sink. Suggested fix: in stopBed and evictCues, once the fade is due (or at once when currentTime has not moved), disconnect the bed's gain and its source and gain nodes so they stop holding buffers. Evidence: _harness/_reports/fw_r4_mem_bitmaps_ret*.log (retainer chains), fw_r4_mem_final_high_device.json vs fw_r4_mem_final_high.json, and the clock reading in fw_r4_mem_track.js.

items.id: UI-1 reproduce and find the cause of the Esc / Leave match timeout
items.evidence:
Reproduced in the production client: vite build into _harness/_prod/fw_r4_ui/dist, served by vite preview, real Chrome on the GPU, no dev handle. Used the same inputs as the probe: minimap right click, the skill-point click, the mouse to the middle, then Q W E R every 3 s. Tool: _harness/fw_r4_ui_leave.mjs.

CAUSE: a targeted ability was being aimed when Esc was pressed. With quickCast off (the default), Q, W, E or R on a learned, ready ability enters aiming. src/input/controller.ts:250 takes Esc in the window capture phase: it cancels the aim and calls stopImmediatePropagation. So the first Esc only cancels the aim and the match menu does not open. The probe pressed Esc once and then waited 15 s.

WHY IT HAPPENED IN ONLY SOME RUNS: the probe's .aslot__lvl click (timeout 1000 ms) usually fails because the '+' button bobs (hud.css animation), so skill points mostly go unspent. In fp1 at 5:10 the player is level 4 with 3 points unspent, and most key presses are refused with no aim.

RUNS (load 2.6 at the first start, 64 to 479 for the rest, all from other processes):
- 3 runs with no forced aim (run1, trials1, fp1; fp1 also had the probe's footprint polls): 6 of 6 leaves opened the menu on the first Esc.
- Within those runs, 117 of 117 trials opened the menu on the first Esc, and 0 of those trials had an aim.
- Forced-aim run (--aim --footprint --sec 200; Ctrl+Q/E/R learn the abilities, then a key puts one in aim): 13 of 13 aimed trials gave no menu on Esc 1, the aim was cleared (aimAfter1 = 0), and Esc 2 opened the menu every time. 6 of 6 unaimed trials opened it on Esc 1. 19 of 19 menus closed again with Esc.
- The final RIFT leave of that run showed the exact probe symptom. Before Esc, 'Bear Down' (Q) was being aimed (cur-aim). Esc 1: no menu for 15 s, the range ring gone. Esc 2: menu.

SHOTS:
- _harness/_shots/fw_r4_ui_leave_aim1_rift_before_esc.png
- _harness/_shots/fw_r4_ui_leave_aim1_rift_esc1_timeout.png

REPORTS (each holds a per-press Escape log, with consumed=true on Esc 1 in the aim cases):
- _harness/_reports/fw_r4_ui_leave_run1.json
- _harness/_reports/fw_r4_ui_leave_trials1.json
- _harness/_reports/fw_r4_ui_leave_fp1.json
- _harness/_reports/fw_r4_ui_leave_aim1.json

The other suspects were ruled out by the DOM state recorded at every press: 0 modals, shop closed, no ping wheel, focus on body. No dismissable modal or shop took the press.

VERDICT: no client change. Esc cancels targeting first and a second Esc opens the menu, which is the usual RTS/MOBA behaviour; it was reliable in 14 of 14 cases (13 trials and the final leave). The HUD's menu button is also always there as a mouse path.
